executive_summary.text: Microsoft shipped a record 622 CVEs in its July 2026 Patch Tuesday — more than triple June's previous high — with two actively exploited zero-days in ADFS (CVE-2026-56155) and SharePoint Server (CVE-2026-56164) that demand immediate patching.

CISA imposed a July 19 (Saturday) KEV remediation deadline on five actively exploited flaws spanning Fortinet FortiSandbox, SharePoint RCE, Oracle E-Business Suite, and SonicWall SMA 1000 — the latter two rated CVSS 9.8 and 10.0.

Identity-centric attacks on Microsoft 365 and Entra ID dominated the cycle, with the Forg365 phishing-as-a-service platform, OAuth Client ID spoofing, and ShinyHunters SaaS OAuth abuse all targeting the trust organizations have already extended to connected apps.

A ransomware attack on Coca-Cola's Fairlife dairy subsidiary halted US production, while Japanese frozen-food giant Nichirei and consultancy Ernst & Young separately disclosed disruptive breaches — underscoring continued operational impact from financially motivated intrusions.

Two Scattered Spider leaders were sentenced to 66 months in the UK for the £29 million Transport for London hack, and Expel attributed the April DigiCert breach to a GoldenEyeDog subgroup (CylindricalCanine) that stole code-signing certificates.

cyber_news.title: Microsoft Patches Record 622 CVEs in July 2026 Patch Tuesday
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft shipped its largest Patch Tuesday on record, covering 622 of its own CVEs — more than triple June's previous high of roughly 200 — including two zero-days already under active exploitation in ADFS and SharePoint Server.
cyber_news.expanded: The two actively exploited zero-days are CVE-2026-56155, an insufficient access-control granularity flaw in Active Directory Federation Services allowing an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally, and CVE-2026-56164, a missing-authentication-for-critical-function bug in SharePoint Server enabling an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over the network. Microsoft attributed the ballooning patch count to vulnerability discoveries aided by artificial intelligence, and CrowdStrike's analysis flagged the exponential increase as a new triage reality. Cisco Talos released accompanying Snort rules for the most prominent vulnerabilities in the release.

cyber_news.title: CISA Slams July 19 KEV Deadline on Five Actively Exploited Flaws
cyber_news.summary: CISA added five actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a July 19 remediation deadline, spanning Fortinet FortiSandbox, Microsoft SharePoint, Oracle E-Business Suite, and SonicWall SMA 1000.
cyber_news.expanded: The FortiSandbox pair (CVE-2026-25089 and CVE-2026-39808) are unauthenticated OS command injection flaws exploitable via crafted HTTP requests. The separately patched SharePoint RCE CVE-2026-58644 (CVSS 9.8) is a deserialization-of-untrusted-data bug allowing an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network, exploited in the wild within days of disclosure. Oracle EBS CVE-2026-46817 enables unauthenticated takeover of Oracle Payments via HTTP. The two SonicWall SMA 1000 zero-days — CVE-2026-15409 (CVSS 10.0 SSRF) and CVE-2026-15410 (code injection enabling admin-level OS command execution) — were chained by attackers against exposed appliances.

cyber_news.title: Forg365 PhaaS Platform Targets Microsoft 365 with Device Code Phishing and AitM Session Theft
cyber_news.summary: A new phishing-as-a-service operation called Forg365 is combining device code phishing, adversary-in-the-middle session theft, AI-assisted lure creation, and post-compromise mailbox manipulation to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts, sold via Telegram for $400/month.
cyber_news.expanded: Forg365's attack chains begin with device code phishing that abuses the OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant, prompting targets to enter a code at a legitimate Microsoft login endpoint — sidestepping many conditional access and MFA controls that expect a browser flow. AitM proxies then intercept the resulting session token in real time, defeating phishing-resistant MFA by replaying the stolen session. Post-compromise modules perform mailbox operations such as inbox rule creation and mail forwarding to maintain persistence and exfiltrate data while evading alerting. The integration of AI for lure generation and antibot evasion marks a maturation of the PhaaS market targeting the Microsoft 365 estate specifically.

cyber_news.title: OAuth Client ID Spoofing Lets Attackers Validate Stolen Entra ID Credentials Stealthily
cyber_news.summary: At least two threat actors are weaponizing a novel OAuth Client ID spoofing technique to enumerate accounts and validate stolen Microsoft Entra ID credentials without generating a successful sign-in event that would alert defenders.
cyber_news.expanded: The technique abuses the way Entra ID records authentication telemetry for certain OAuth flows: by presenting a spoofed client ID alongside stolen credentials, the attacker triggers validation attempts that fail closed but still reveal whether the credential is valid — effectively turning the identity provider into an oracle. Because no successful sign-in is ever recorded, conditional access and identity-protection analytics that key off successful or interactive sign-ins never fire. Microsoft and independent researchers flagged the activity as enabling silent credential stuffing and account enumeration against cloud tenants, with the spoofed client IDs often impersonating first-party Microsoft applications to blend into expected traffic.

cyber_news.title: ShinyHunters Walks Into Salesforce Environments via Trusted OAuth Connections
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence mapped three Salesforce attack paths tied to a year of ShinyHunters activity, where attackers entered corporate Salesforce tenants without exploiting any platform flaw — instead abusing the OAuth connections and guest access the organization had already extended to third-party apps.
cyber_news.expanded: The three documented paths leverage vishing, supply-chain compromise, and misconfigured guest access to obtain or reuse OAuth tokens that already held legitimate scope inside the Salesforce tenant. Once armed with a trusted OAuth grant, ShinyHunters queried and exiltrated data through the platform's own APIs, generating activity that looked like normal integration traffic. Microsoft emphasized that the abuse is fundamentally a problem of over-permissioned, unmonitored OAuth grants in SaaS — the trust boundary is the integration, not the perimeter — and that detection requires auditing consent grants and token usage patterns rather than relying on sign-in anomaly logic alone.

cyber_news.title: ACR Stealer Uses ClickFix Lures to Steal Browser Tokens and Microsoft 365 Files
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft Defender Experts detailed two intrusion chains used by the ACR Stealer infostealer, which has been walking out of enterprise networks with saved browser passwords, live session tokens, and files from synced OneDrive and SharePoint folders since late April 2026.
cyber_news.expanded: ACR Stealer's delivery relies on the ClickFix social-engineering pattern: victims are tricked into pasting a malicious command into the Windows Run box or Terminal, which fetches and executes the payload without traditional dropper binaries that EDR signatures catch. Once running, the stealer harvests browser-stored credentials and live session cookies — bypassing MFA on already-authenticated sessions — and enumerates synced OneDrive and SharePoint folders for document exfiltration. Microsoft observed two distinct intrusion chains converging on the same payload family, indicating the stealer is being rented or sold across multiple affiliate operations, which explains the breadth of activity from late April through mid-June.

cyber_news.title: GoldenEyeDog Subgroup Linked to DigiCert Breach and Code-Signing Certificate Theft
cyber_news.summary: Expel attributed the April 2026 DigiCert security incident to a threat cluster dubbed CylindricalCanine, described as a subgroup of the Chinese cybercrime group GoldenEyeDog (aka APT-Q-27, Dragon Breath, Miuuti Group), which stole code-signing certificates.
cyber_news.expanded: GoldenEyeDog has historically targeted the gambling and gaming sectors, but the DigiCert intrusion represents a pivot toward supply-chain value: code-signing certificates stolen from a major certificate authority let the attacker sign binaries that pass OS trust checks and Gatekeeper validation, enabling downstream malware to masquerade as legitimate software. Expel's technical writeup traced the activity cluster through overlapping infrastructure and tradecraft markers tying CylindricalCanine back to the parent group. The breach's significance lies less in the immediate data loss than in the downstream risk that stolen signing material poses to the broader software ecosystem until revocation and re-issuance complete.

cyber_news.title: Scattered Spider Leaders Sentenced to 66 Months for £29M TfL Hack
cyber_news.summary: Two leading members of the Scattered Spider subset of The Com — Owen Flowers, 18, and Thalha Jubair, 20 — were sentenced to five and a half years at Woolwich Crown Court for the 2024 Transport for London hack that left 148 systems inoperable and forced all 27,000 TfL employees to reset passwords in person.
cyber_news.expanded: The TfL attack exemplified Scattered Spider's trademark identity-based social engineering: the group manipulated help desks and abused MFA fatigue and SIM-swapping techniques to pivot from initial access into deep enterprise compromise, ultimately rendering 148 systems inoperable. U.S. authorities had previously accused Jubair of participating in at least 120 attacks. The NCA and CPS placed TfL's losses and recovery costs at tens of millions of pounds, and the judge cited the pair's 'selfish bravado.' The sentencing closes a chapter on one of the most disruptive UK public-sector intrusions in recent years and signals continued law enforcement pressure on The Com's UK contingent.

cyber_news.title: n8n Token Exchange Flaw Logs Attackers In as Users From Another Issuer
cyber_news.summary: The n8n workflow automation platform handed out the wrong accounts at login on Enterprise instances configured to trust more than one external token issuer, matching an incoming JWT to a local user on the sub claim alone while ignoring the iss claim.
cyber_news.expanded: A valid token from issuer A carrying a sub that belonged to a user under issuer B logged the attacker in as that user — their password never entered the picture. The root cause is a classic JWT validation defect: the verifier honored the subject claim but failed to enforce issuer binding, so any trusted issuer could mint a token impersonating another issuer's user population. On multi-tenant or federated n8n Enterprise deployments, this collapses tenant boundaries at the authentication layer. The flaw illustrates a recurring class of OIDC implementation bugs where partial claim validation creates cross-issuer impersonation primitives, and it required n8n to ship fixes enforcing iss matching across all configured trust chains.

cyber_news.title: Three Chained Siemens ROX II Zero-Days Grant Persistent Root on OT Switches
cyber_news.summary: Palo Alto Unit 42 published a technical analysis of three chained zero-day vulnerabilities in Siemens ROX II OT switches that together allow privilege escalation and persistent root access to industrial network equipment.
cyber_news.expanded: The 'three steps to the terminal' chain moves from an initial access primitive through privilege escalation to a persistent root shell on the ROX II device, which sits in industrial control networks where persistence can survive firmware refreshes if not fully scrubbed. OT switches like these are typically long-lived, lightly-monitored, and trusted by adjacent engineering workstations, so a rooted switch becomes a durable foothold for lateral movement, traffic manipulation, or staging attacks against higher-value ICS assets. The disclosure underscores that OT-specific network gear carries exploitable firmware logic that mainstream IT patch cadences rarely reach, and that defenders should treat OT switching infrastructure as a privileged attack surface rather than passive plumbing.

cyber_news.title: Identity Attacks Overtake Exploits as Top Ransomware Root Cause
cyber_news.summary: Sophos incident-response research found that phishing, brute force, and other identity-based threats surpassed software vulnerabilities as the leading means of delivering ransomware last year, with MFA deployed in 97% of credential-based attacks yet failing to prevent compromise.
cyber_news.expanded: The data reframes the ransomware entry problem: it is now predominantly an identity problem rather than an unpatched-software problem. The finding that MFA was present in nearly all credential-based compromises yet did not stop them aligns with the rise of AitM proxies, MFA fatigue, and SIM-swap techniques that defeat second-factor checks after credentials are obtained. The implication for defenders is that identity hardening — phishing-resistant MFA (passkeys, FIDO2), session-token protection, and conditional access tuned to impossible-travel and token-theft signals — now outranks patch velocity as the dominant ransomware control, even as Patch Tuesday volumes hit record highs.

cyber_news.title: ClickLock macOS Stealer Kills Apps Every 210ms Until Victims Type Their Password
cyber_news.summary: A new macOS infostealer dubbed ClickLock terminates all visible processes on a loop to force victims into entering their system login password, arriving as a Terminal command behind a fake system dialog and persisting via two LaunchAgents.
cyber_news.expanded: ClickLock's coercion loop kills Finder, the Dock, Spotlight, Terminal, Activity Monitor, and other foreground apps approximately every 210 milliseconds, making the machine unusable until the victim enters their password into the attacker's fake prompt — a pressure tactic borrowed from Windows-era screen-locker malware but newly effective on macOS where users have fewer escape hatches. On the next login, the LaunchAgents reactivate and harvest the stored login keychain password, browser cookies, and session data. The ClickFix delivery vector (pasting a command into Terminal) and the abuse of legitimate LaunchAgent persistence reflect a broader 2026 trend of macOS stealers moving past Gatekeeper using notarized droppers and native C++ implementations rather than AppleScript wrappers.

deep_dive.title: Microsoft July 2026 Patch Tuesday: Record 622 CVEs and Two Actively Exploited Zero-Days
deep_dive.content: Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday is the largest on record, covering 622 of the company's own CVEs by its Security Update Guide count — more than triple June's previous high of roughly 200 — a surge Microsoft attributes to vulnerability discoveries aided by artificial intelligence. Two of the fixes close holes already under active exploitation, both credited to incident responders. CVE-2026-56155 is an insufficient access-control granularity flaw in Active Directory Federation Services that lets an authorized attacker elevate privileges locally, while CVE-2026-56164 is a missing-authentication-for-critical-function vulnerability in SharePoint Server allowing an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network. Compounding the SharePoint exposure, a separate, newly patched deserialization RCE (CVE-2026-58644, CVSS 9.8) was added to CISA's KEV catalog with a July 19 deadline after being exploited in the wild within days of disclosure. CrowdStrike's analysis and Cisco Talos's accompanying Snort rules flagged the exponential increase as a new triage reality for defenders. The release affects virtually every Microsoft shop, and the two live zero-days — both privilege-elevation primitives ideal for post-initial-access movement — are the priority fixes, with the broader 622-CVE backlog forcing hard prioritization given the volume.

biggest_hacks.title: Coca-Cola Fairlife ransomware attack halts US dairy production
biggest_hacks.summary: A ransomware attack on Coca-Cola's Fairlife dairy subsidiary disrupted operations and temporarily suspended production of Fairlife products across the United States, with the full scope still undetermined.

biggest_hacks.title: Ernst & Young discloses data breach after third-party support system hack
biggest_hacks.summary: Ernst & Young is notifying customers of a data breach caused by the compromise of a third-party support ticket system used by its IT personnel, exposing data handled through that support channel.

biggest_hacks.title: DigiCert breach attributed to GoldenEyeDog subgroup; code-signing certificates stolen
biggest_hacks.summary: Expel attributed the April 2026 DigiCert incident to a GoldenEyeDog subgroup dubbed CylindricalCanine, which stole code-signing certificates that could be used to sign malicious binaries as legitimate software.

biggest_hacks.title: Japanese frozen-food giant Nichirei disrupted by cyberattack
biggest_hacks.summary: Japanese frozen-food giant Nichirei disconnected its systems on July 13 following a cyberattack and is gradually restoring operations after the disruption to its production and logistics.

biggest_hacks.title: 23andMe agrees to $18m settlement with 43 attorneys general over genetics breach
biggest_hacks.summary: 23andMe agreed to pay $18 million and adopt enhanced data protection requirements to settle claims with a coalition of 43 attorneys general over its 2023 genetics data breach.

biggest_hacks.title: Lidl notifies customers of third-party supplier data breach
biggest_hacks.summary: Supermarket giant Lidl disclosed a supplier breach impacting customer data, adding to the run of third-party supply-chain compromises affecting major brands this cycle.
